reasons: Run failures are caught and reported to the user.
Blank or partial numbers are not checked before they reach the store and the backend.

terms.meaning: Energy storage system, a battery added to the solar system.
Balance of system, the non-panel parts of a solar installation such as racking, wiring and transformers.
Operations and maintenance, the yearly costs of keeping the system running.
Kilowatts of panel (DC) capacity and kilowatts of grid-side (AC) capacity.
The panel capacity divided by the inverter capacity.
A decimal between 0 and 1, so 0.05 means 5 percent.
The exact name a value is stored under, which must match the backend's name for it.

depends_on: backend/schemas/inputs.py (field names come from here, per the code comment)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and input types
sections.what: Brings in the data shapes for each input group, the store, the notification tool, icons, and the Button component.
sections.why: Each group has its own shape so the editor can check the right fields are used.
sections.watch_out: The data shapes must match the groups defined here; renaming on one side breaks the form.

sections.name: InputSection
sections.title: Section names list
sections.what: Lists the nine input group names the form can open: system, modules, inverters, ess, sbos, ebos, labor, other, and om.
sections.why: Fixing the names means a typo cannot create a section that does not exist.
sections.watch_out: A new group must be added here, to the display code, and to the store together.

sections.name: InputPanel (part 1)
sections.title: Panel state and actions
sections.what: Sets up the link to the store, the open or closed state of each section (system and modules start open), and the three actions: run, export, and reset, each with its own success and error messages.
sections.why: Likely reason: starting the two most-used sections open makes the long form less intimidating.
sections.watch_out: Run Analysis always requests lecture and research content, and this screen offers no way to turn them off.

sections.name: InputPanel (part 2)
sections.title: Top action bar and layout start
sections.what: Shows nothing until inputs exist. Then draws the title, the Reset, Export and Run Analysis buttons, and starts the section list with the system section.
sections.why: Likely reason: the top bar keeps the main actions in one place at the top of the form.
sections.watch_out: Export's greyed-out state is read directly from the store while drawing, which is a different pattern from the rest of the file, so it may be harder to follow.

sections.name: InputPanel (part 3)
sections.title: Modules through BOS sections
sections.what: Shows the solar modules, inverters, energy storage, structural BOS, and electrical BOS sections, each wired so a change goes into its own input group.
sections.why: Each section passes its own group name, so changes land in the right place.
sections.watch_out: A copy-and-paste mistake in a group name would put values into the wrong group with no error.

sections.name: InputPanel (part 4)
sections.title: Labor through O&M sections
sections.what: Shows the labor, other costs, and operations and maintenance sections, wired the same way as the earlier sections.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same wiring pattern keeps the sections consistent.

sections.name: InputSectionProps
sections.title: Section box settings shape
sections.what: Describes what one collapsible section needs: its title, open flag, toggle action, and content.
sections.why: Keeps the section box reusable.

sections.name: InputSection
sections.title: Collapsible section box
sections.what: Draws one collapsible box with a clickable header. The content slides open or closed over about 0.15 seconds.
sections.why: Likely reason: collapsing sections keeps the long form readable.
sections.watch_out: Closed content is hidden rather than removed, so its values stay in memory even when the box is closed.

sections.name: FieldSpec
sections.title: Number field description
sections.what: Describes one numeric field: its stored name, label, and optional minimum, maximum, and step size.
sections.why: Keeps each field defined in one simple row so the lists are easy to scan.
sections.watch_out: The stored name must match the backend's name exactly, or the value will not reach the right place.

sections.name: SYSTEM_FIELDS
sections.title: System sizing fields
sections.what: Lists the three system-level numbers: system size in kWdc, the DC to AC ratio (ILR), and storage duration in hours per kWdc.
sections.why: These are the basic sizing values that the rest of the model builds on.

sections.name: MODULE_FIELDS
sections.title: Solar module fields
sections.what: Lists the panel values: efficiency, cost range per watt, panel height, width and weight, annual factory capacity, labor hours, electricity use, depreciation years, and yearly maintenance rate.
sections.why: Likely reason: panel details drive the module cost and the area estimate on the diagram.
sections.watch_out: Efficiency and maintenance rate are fractions between 0 and 1, but the number box may still accept a value such as 5 for 5 percent.

sections.name: INVERTER_FIELDS
sections.title: Inverter fields
sections.what: Lists inverter cost ranges per kWac, annual capacity, labor hours per kWac, depreciation years, and efficiency.
sections.why: Likely reason: inverter cost is priced per kWac, so the values are kept in that unit.
sections.watch_out: The inverter type dropdown is built separately in another part of the form, not in this list.

sections.name: ESS_FIELDS
sections.title: Energy storage fields
sections.what: Lists battery cost per kWh, fixed project cost, incentive per kWh, round-trip efficiency, and lifetime cycles.
sections.why: Likely reason: battery cost is split into a per-energy rate and a fixed project amount.
sections.watch_out: Round-trip efficiency is a fraction, so enter 0.85 rather than 85.

sections.name: SBOS_FIELDS
sections.title: Structural BOS fields
sections.what: Lists racking area per kWdc and the tracker and fixed racking cost ranges per square metre.
sections.why: Racking cost is calculated from area, so area and cost are entered together.
sections.watch_out: Costs are per square metre while area is per kWdc, so a unit mix-up here changes the totals.

sections.name: EBOS_FIELDS
sections.title: Electrical BOS fields
sections.what: Lists cost ranges for the transformer, breakers, combiner box and wiring, plus shipping and tariff rates as fractions.
sections.why: Likely reason: electrical equipment is priced in parts so each can be adjusted separately.
sections.watch_out: Transformer and breaker costs are per kWac, while combiner and wiring costs are per kWdc, and mixing these up skews the total.

sections.name: LABOR_FIELDS
sections.title: Labor fields
sections.what: Lists field and office hourly rates, hours per kWdc for each, and a labor burden fraction.
sections.why: Labor is split between field and office work so each can have its own rate.
sections.watch_out: Labor burden is a fraction, not a percentage.

sections.name: OTHER_FIELDS
sections.title: Other cost fields
sections.what: Lists sales tax, contingency, management overhead, and developer profit, each as a fraction.
sections.why: Likely reason: these are percentage add-ons applied to the cost total.
sections.watch_out: Each value is a fraction between 0 and 1, so 0.07 means 7 percent.

sections.name: OM_FIELDS
sections.title: Operations and maintenance fields
sections.what: Lists yearly cost ranges for cleaning, inspection, replacement, insurance, property tax, and land lease, plus the discount rate.
sections.why: The results label O&M as NPV, so the discount rate turns future yearly costs into today's money.
sections.watch_out: Insurance and property tax are fractions of capital cost, while cleaning and the others are per kWdc per year, so check units before editing.

sections.name: FieldGridProps
sections.title: Grid layout settings shape
sections.what: Describes what the shared grid needs: the list of fields, the current values, the change action, and optional extra boxes shown first.
sections.why: Lets one grid layout serve every section.

sections.name: FieldGrid
sections.title: Shared number grid
sections.what: Lays out the number boxes in a grid of one column on phones and up to four on wide screens. Any extra dropdown appears first, then one box per field, showing the current value or blank.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single shared layout keeps every section looking the same.
sections.watch_out: A missing value shows as a blank box, which is easy to miss and may send an empty value.

sections.name: SystemInputsForm
sections.title: System section form
sections.what: Shows the three system fields in the shared grid.
sections.why: Each section form is a thin wrapper so the shared grid does the work.

sections.name: ModuleInputsForm
sections.title: Module section form
sections.what: Shows the module fields in the shared grid.
sections.why: Same thin-wrapper pattern as the other sections.

sections.name: InverterInputsForm
sections.title: Inverter section form
sections.what: Shows the inverter fields plus a dropdown for inverter type: central, string, or micro.
sections.why: Likely reason: the inverter type is limited to a fixed list rather than free text.
sections.watch_out: If a saved type is not one of these three, the dropdown will show the first choice while the stored value stays different.

sections.name: ESSInputsForm
sections.title: Storage section form
sections.what: Shows the storage fields plus a dropdown that switches between PV only and PV plus storage.
sections.why: This dropdown turns storage on or off for the run.
sections.watch_out: Switching to PV only changes the flag but keeps the storage numbers filled in and stored.

sections.name: SBOSInputsForm
sections.title: Racking section form
sections.what: Shows the racking fields plus a dropdown for single-axis tracker or fixed tilt.
sections.why: Likely reason: the choice decides which racking cost range is used.
sections.watch_out: Both the tracker and fixed cost ranges stay in the input, so switching the dropdown does not erase the other option's numbers.

sections.name: EBOSInputsForm
sections.title: Electrical BOS section form
sections.what: Shows the electrical BOS fields in the shared grid.
sections.why: Same thin-wrapper pattern as the other sections.

sections.name: LaborInputsForm
sections.title: Labor section form
sections.what: Shows the labor fields in the shared grid.
sections.why: Same thin-wrapper pattern as the other sections.

sections.name: OtherInputsForm
sections.title: Other costs section form
sections.what: Shows the other cost fields in the shared grid.
sections.why: Same thin-wrapper pattern as the other sections.

sections.name: OMInputsForm
sections.title: O&M section form
sections.what: Shows the operations and maintenance fields in the shared grid.
sections.why: Same thin-wrapper pattern as the other sections.

sections.name: SectionFormProps
sections.title: Section form settings shape
sections.what: Describes what each section form needs: its values and the change action.
sections.why: One shared shape lets the same rules work for all nine groups.
sections.watch_out: The values are loosely typed, so the editor will not catch a value of the wrong type.

sections.name: InputFieldProps
sections.title: Number box settings shape
sections.what: Describes one number box: its label, input type, value, change action, and optional limits and step size.
sections.why: Keeps the number box's inputs in one clear description.
sections.watch_out: The minimum, maximum and step values only guide the browser's arrows and checks; they do not stop a typed value from being saved.

sections.name: InputField
sections.title: Number box drawing
sections.what: Draws one labelled number box. A complete number is passed on as a number. Partial entries such as an empty box, a lone minus sign, or a lone decimal point are passed on as text so the user can keep typing.
sections.why: Likely reason: letting the user type a minus sign or decimal point without the box clearing.
sections.watch_out: Those partial text values can reach the store and the backend, so the run must handle or block them.

sections.name: SelectFieldProps
sections.title: Dropdown settings shape
sections.what: Describes one dropdown: its label, current choice, change action, and list of choices.
sections.why: Keeps dropdowns built the same way.

sections.name: SelectField
sections.title: Dropdown drawing
sections.what: Draws a labelled dropdown that passes the chosen value on as text.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single dropdown style keeps every choice looking alike.
sections.watch_out: Dropdown values arrive as text, so any conversion to yes or no flags happens in the calling section, not here.

summary: The input form: nine collapsible sections where the user enters the solar system's sizes, costs, rates and financial assumptions, plus buttons to reset, export and run the analysis.
purpose: Lets the user change every assumption the cost model uses, then start a run.
why: Likely reason: grouping inputs into sections keeps a long list manageable, and the field lists keep each label and limit in one place.
how: Shows nine collapsible sections. Each section is built from a list of field descriptions (label, field name, minimum, maximum, step size). Every change is sent to the store's updateInput with the group name and field name. Run Analysis asks for lecture and research content, then reports success or failure with a pop-up. Reset reloads the defaults. Export stays greyed out until outputs exist.
inputs: What the user types or selects in the form. Store values: inputs, outputs, calculating, and exporting. Field names that follow the backend's input schema.
outputs: Updated inputs in the store, a run request, a downloaded Excel file, and pop-up messages.
risks: Partial numbers such as an empty box, a lone minus sign, or a lone decimal point are passed on as text. Reset replaces all inputs without asking for confirmation.
debug: If a run fails with the check your inputs message, look for blank or partial number boxes. If a value does not save, check that its field name matches the backend schema file named in the code comment. If Export stays greyed out, no run has produced outputs yet.
